text:
maya: Noticed a new p95 blip on the hosted ingress after yesterday's kernel-weight tweak. Spike started ~11:07 UTC on canary traffic. Anyone else?

samir: Saw it in the canary dashboard. P95 up ~110ms for small-turn conversations (~20-150 tokens). Traces point to host parse + tokenize time.

maya: Quick flame sample shows a lot of syscall noise around writev and repeated proto unmarshal. Short stack: parse_request -> tokenize -> kv_lookup -> grpc_writev.

samir: Also observed reduced KV prefix reuse on these traces. Hit-rate dropped from ~86% -> 79% on the affected shard after kernel hint change. Possible chunk boundary shift.

alicia: If chunking changed we might be splitting common prefixes. Small requests are sensitive to that. We should test a temporary prefix-preserve heuristic (keep last 6-10 tokens as a single cache key). Low risk A/B.

jon: I instrumented ingress packets: lots of 200-500B frames over HTTP2. HPACK table churn + many small writes causing syscalls. Coalescing window at 200us currently.

ryan: Repro plan: spin the small-request workload (1k qps, 70% small) against a canary with two toggles: (1) revert kernel-weight change, (2) coalesce window -> 600us.

samir: Microbench showed coalesce 200->600us drops writev syscalls by ~2.8x and parse CPU by ~8% on small workload. End-to-end smoke p95 improvement ~60-100ms in local run.

maya: Nice. Any risk of added latency for larger requests?

samir: Minimal based on warmup runs. We only delay by a few hundred microseconds; batching helps amortize overhead for small requests. For long seqs it'll be a no-op because they stream more frames.

alicia: I'll prototype the prefix-preserve patch and add unit tests for key normalization. Suggest N=8 tokens default.

jon: Also check kernel selector minibatch policy: hint change might bias toward smaller minibatches. If selector prefers tiny minibatches for this traffic mix, tokenization overhead becomes dominant. We can add a bias term for small-seq workloads to nudge toward minibatch size 8-12.

maya: I opened a quick canary PR for coalesce window behind a flag: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/4337

ci-bot: Build green. Canary plan: deploy to shard s-23 with flag coalesce_us=600 and kernel-weight revert enabled on that shard.

ryan: Deployed. Early metrics (3m): p95 down ~50ms vs bad canary; writev count down ~2.5x; HPACK retransmit simplified. KV hit-rate creeping up to 82%.

samir: Good sign. I'll run the batch-bias experiment next and post results. Config snippet I'm trying:
```json
{"workload":"small-chat","batch_bias":1.3,"minibatch_target":10}
```

alicia: PR for prefix-preserve is in draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/ingress/pulls/4338. Tests added for normalization and existing cache invariants.

jon: Actions captured:
- samir: run batch-bias perf sweep and share flame graphs (ETA 2h)
- alicia: finalize prefix-preserve PR and include perf microbench (ETA 3h)
- maya: hold canary for 45m and collect traces/metrics (ETA 45m)
- ryan: monitor for regressions and be ready to rollback

maya: Thanks. Early hypothesis = host-side small-write churn (writev/HPACK) + cache fragmentation due to changed chunking. Coalesce + revert gives immediate relief; batching bias + prefix-preserve are next wave for durable fix.

ci-bot: Canary metrics snapshot available: https://metrics.internal/redwood/canaries/6491112222

samir: Preliminary numbers look consistent across two shards. If the next batch-bias run confirms, we can stage promote with a 2hr observation window.

maya: Closing loop later with the performance report. Ping here if you see anomalies. :thumbsup:
